decision.summary: Mains gateway architecture using EFR32MG24 (802.15.4) + dual-band Wi-Fi (5 GHz primary) + BGT60TR13C radar/PIR fusion is conditionally sound, but gates on compute host selection, mmWave calibration spec, and DAC provisioning line setup.
decision.recommendation: Proceed with the decoupled architecture (EFR32MG24 for 802.15.4 mesh/TBR + separate 5 GHz-primary Wi-Fi/BLE + BGT60TR13C radar with PIR fusion for mains gateway; PIR-first Thread Sleepy End Device for battery satellite variant). Hold full architecture freeze until compute host class, mmWave mounting/calibration spec, and factory DAC provisioning are formally resolved.

assumptions.statement: Dual-band Wi-Fi operates primarily on 5 GHz during normal operation, avoiding heavy 2.4 GHz co-located TX interference with the 802.15.4 mesh.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Sustained 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi uploads deafen the 802.15.4 receiver, causing periodic Thread/Zigbee packet drops and latency spikes.

assumptions.statement: Concurrent Zigbee and Thread dynamic multiprotocol operation on a single EFR32MG24 radio can meet latency targets at expected device counts.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Heavy multi-mesh traffic starves radio airtime, leading to dropped messages and degraded Thread Border Router responsiveness.

assumptions.statement: Infineon BGT60TR13C (1TX/3RX) combined with PIR fusion can reliably distinguish 2–3 coarse zones per room after per-install calibration.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Limited 3-RX angular resolution fails to separate close indoor zones, leading to false room/zone triggers.

assumptions.statement: Manufacturing facility can support secure hardware key injection and per-device DAC provisioning required for Matter certification.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Inability to inject Device Attestation Certificates at production scale blocks Matter certification and prevents product release.

assumptions.statement: The overall compute workload (radar DSP, Thread Border Router, Wi-Fi stack, local automations) can be hosted on an MCU-class host without requiring a Linux application processor.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Underestimating processing/memory needs forces a costly late-stage architecture redesign to a Linux host (e.g. i.MX series) with RCP radio topology.

risks.description: In-device 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi TX bursts overwhelm 802.15.4 receiver sensitivity during simultaneous transmission windows.
risks.mitigation: Enforce 5 GHz primary Wi-Fi, implement 3/4-wire hardware PTA coexistence signalling between radios, physically separate antennas, and restrict 802.15.4 to channels 15/20/25/26.

risks.description: Radar false triggers caused by periodic environmental motion (ceiling fans, HVAC vents, moving curtains) trigger unintended automations.
risks.mitigation: Apply Doppler notch filtering, configure presence persistence dwell timers, and require PIR motion-onset corroboration prior to firing actions.

risks.description: Compute starvation on a single MCU core when concurrently processing FMCW range-Doppler FFTs, running Thread Border Router routing, and servicing local automation logic.
risks.mitigation: Formally evaluate MCU DSP/RAM capacity vs Linux Application Host + RCP architecture prior to board layout freeze.

risks.description: Matter / Thread certification schedule slip due to unestablished PKI attestation supply chain (DAC injection) or test house compliance failures.
risks.mitigation: Set up manufacturing DAC injection early and run automated Matter test harness on pre-production engineering samples.

tradeoffs.option: Dedicated 802.15.4 SoC (EFR32MG24) + Separate Wi-Fi/BLE IC vs. Single 2.4GHz Combo SoC
tradeoffs.benefit: Eliminates single-die RF coupling, provides dedicated processing for Thread Border Router, and enables superior physical antenna isolation.
tradeoffs.drawback: Increases total BOM cost, component count, and board surface area.

tradeoffs.option: Radar + PIR Multi-Sensor Fusion vs. Radar-Only Sensing
tradeoffs.benefit: PIR provides fast <100ms motion onset trigger and rejects static radar reflections; mmWave holds stationary presence via micro-motion without camera privacy concerns.
tradeoffs.drawback: Adds secondary sensor BOM cost, housing enclosure window requirements, and extra MCU IO/ADC channels.

tradeoffs.option: Battery Satellite Variant: PIR-First Sleepy End Device vs. Continuous mmWave Radar
tradeoffs.benefit: Allows deep-sleep operation achieving multi-year battery life on AA/coin cells.
tradeoffs.drawback: Loses stationary micro-motion detection on the satellite variant unless periodic low-duty radar sampling is enabled.

evidence.claim: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channels (20–40 MHz wide at ~+20 dBm) blind co-located 802.15.4 receivers (2 MHz wide at 0 to +8 dBm) without band separation or high isolation.
Infineon BGT60TR13C is a 60 GHz 1TX/3RX FMCW radar suitable for room-level micro-motion presence detection.
Operating as a Thread Border Router requires an always-on 802.15.4 radio receiver stack.
Continuous 60 GHz mmWave radar operation draws tens of mA, limiting battery life to days/weeks without duty-cycling or mains power.
EFR32MG24 supports dynamic multiprotocol concurrent Zigbee and Thread operations on a single 802.15.4 radio PHY.

next_actions: Resolve compute host architecture: choose between high-end MCU vs Linux Application Processor (e.g., i.MX 93) with EFR32 running as a Radio Co-Processor (RCP).
Define physical mounting specification (height, tilt) and write the setup calibration algorithm for room zone mapping.
Confirm Matter logo certification scope and finalize the manufacturing line hardware key injection process for Device Attestation Certificates (DACs).
Perform lab PER (Packet Error Rate) coexistence testing under heavy 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi traffic with PTA active on early hardware prototypes.
Execute radar field testing across sample room layouts to validate 1TX/3RX zone separation and optimize fan/pet Doppler rejection filters.
freeze_blockers: Compute host class is unpinned (MCU-only vs Linux host + RCP); selecting an under-resourced core risks complete system architecture rework late in design.
Radar mounting specification and room calibration flow are uncommitted; lack of calibrated boundaries causes wrong-room triggers and field returns.
Matter Device Attestation Certificate (DAC) factory provisioning line and PKI infrastructure are unconfirmed, gating regulatory and logo certification.

traps_caught: 'Matter is a radio' -> it runs over Thread; border-router + cert
mmWave zone detection needs calibration/mounting; false positives
'one SoC does everything' vs radio load / coexistence
judge.rationale: The system flawlessly identified all four domain traps, highlighting RF coexistence (5 GHz primary + PTA), Matter certification/DAC injection over Thread, mmWave radar mounting/calibration requirements with PIR fusion, and compute/radio load constraints (MCU vs Linux RCP architecture). Confidence levels are realistically calibrated to genuine technical uncertainties, and freeze blockers appropriately prevent premature commitment.
